chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from 'Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام how ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday became obligatory, so he said:

Indeed Allah, the Exalted, completed the obligatory salat (prayer) with the supererogatory salat, and He completed the obligatory fasting with the supererogatory fasting, and He completed the obligatory wudu (ablution) with the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday, for whatever may have occurred in that of inadvertence, deficiency, or forgetfulness.

key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory salat prescribed by Allah
key_terms.صَلَاةِ النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory salat that completes deficiencies in obligatory worship
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجُمُعَةِ: the ritual bath associated with Friday
key_terms.وَاجِبًا: obligatory; described here in the wording of the question
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory wudu connected to required acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Why is ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday given special importance in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday serves as a completion for deficiencies connected to obligatory wudu (ablution), just as supererogatory acts complete deficiencies in obligatory salat (prayer) and fasting. It presents a legal and devotional rationale for the special status of Friday ghusl within acts of worship.
